subject: Equality constraints and degrees of freedom

messages.author: bdf1100457a62f70
messages.subject: Equality constraints and degrees of freedom
parts:
Dear lavaan users,

I have a simple question. Does adding equality constraint increase the degrees of freedom?

I have a single indicator auto-regressive cross-lagged panel model, and I found that adding constraints increase the number of degrees of freedom in lavaan.

However, a person in SEMNET believed it to be otherwise (i.e. constraining the paths of IV1->DV2 and IV2->DV3 to be equal reduce the degrees of freedom, but he does not seem to use lavaan.

Best regards,
Edo

messages.subject: Re: Equality constraints and degrees of freedom

Sorry guys! I figured it out! Adding equality constraints do increase the degrees of freedom.
At least according to this website: http://support.sas.com/documentation/cdl/en/statug/67523/HTML/default/viewer.htm#statug_calis_details163.htm#statug_calis027647

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Equality constraints and degrees of freedom
parts: The difference is not lavaan vs other factor-based SEM software, but factor-based SEM vs regression. In regression's F test, the DF in the numerator increase as free parameters are added, but in factor-based SEM's chi-square statistic, DF decline as free parameters are added.  In either technique, imposing an equality constraint reduces the number of free parameters.
